profile.headline: Senior Web Developer at Salt Lake City Corporation
profile.geoLocationName: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
profile.summary:
Queer Web Developer/Software Engineer with hyperfocus superpowers and over a decade of professional programming experience. BA in CS and CompTIA Security+ certified. Skilled in AI Prompt Engineering.

Offers an excellent variety of soft skills along with an aptitude for project planning and management, spreadsheet/dashboard/user flow and workflow/report creation rabies (organizing and planning is my jam), a passion for A11Y, and a genuine love of programming and puzzle solving.

Prefers companies that value respect for their employees, diversity, inclusion, pay equity, celebrating differences, and lets their employees put their pronouns in their email signatures.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Software testing for embedded systems
• Various script fixes and enhancements in MATLAB, C++, C#, XML, XSLT, and HTML
• Peer Review, SCCB, and customer meetings
• Software deployment/release
• Network/Machine/PLN administration internship

positions.title: Precision Electro-Mechanical Assembler
positions.description:
• Precision assembly of navigation systems specializing in fiber optics.
• Chemical/UV handling/safety
• J-STD 001C & IPC 620A soldering
• Teamwork/leadership skills/area auditor

volunteerExperiences.description: I served in the role of Conference Chair for the League of Utah Writers, a nonprofit that supports the writing community in Utah. I headed the League’s Conference Committee, which runs their two main conferences every year, Pre-Quill (one day) and Quills (four days).

volunteerExperiences.role: Hopper Volunteer at the Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing
volunteerExperiences.companyName: Anita Borg Institute for Women in Technology
volunteerExperiences.description: I helped with crowd-control and giving out conference info and directions to attendees at the large Keynote events at the Toyota Center in Houston for the conference. I also helped direct attendees to their panels in the conference at the George R. Brown Convention Center, I welcomed attendees, handed out pins, and gave info for the LGBTQ-A Lunch. It is a great conference and working it makes the experience even better. I look forward to it every year.
